claim: Hydrolysis of nucleoside triphosphates releases similar amounts of energy.
source: Hydrolysis of nucleoside triphosphates releases similar amounts of energy.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle in the abstract without specific experimental data from this manuscript, but is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: ATP hydrolysis is typically used for energy-intensive reactions.
source: ATP hydrolysis is typically used for energy-intensive reactions, whereas GTP hydrolysis typically functions as a switch.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and introduction.

claim: GTP hydrolysis typically functions as a switch.
source: ATP hydrolysis is typically used for energy-intensive reactions, whereas GTP hydrolysis typically functions as a switch.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and introduction.

claim: SpoIVA is a bacterial cytoskeletal protein that hydrolyzes ATP to polymerize irreversibly during Bacillus subtilis sporulation.
source: SpoIVA is a bacterial cytoskeletal protein that hydrolyzes ATP to polymerize irreversibly during Bacillus subtilis sporulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous work (Ramamurthi and Losick, 2008; Roels et al., 1992).

claim: SpoIVA evolved from a TRAFAC class of P-loop GTPases.
source: SpoIVA evolved from a TRAFAC class of P-loop GTPases, but the evolutionary pressure that drove this change in nucleotide specificity is unclear.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by previous work (Castaing et al., 2013; Leipe et al., 2002).

claim: SpoIVAGTPase functioned properly as a GTPase but failed to polymerize because it did not form an NDP-bound intermediate that is required for polymerization.
source: SpoIVAGTPase functioned properly as a GTPase but failed to polymerize because it did not form an NDP-bound intermediate that we report is required for polymerization.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2, 4, and 5.

claim: Incubation of SpoIVAGTPase with limiting ATP did not promote efficient polymerization.
source: Further, incubation of SpoIVAGTPase with limiting ATP did not promote efficient polymerization.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The nucleotide base, in addition to the energy released from hydrolysis, can be critical in specific biological functions.
source: This approach revealed that the nucleotide base, in addition to the energy released from hydrolysis, can be critical in specific biological functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Increased levels of ATP relative to GTP at the end of sporulation was the evolutionary pressure that drove the change in nucleotide preference in SpoIVA.
source: We also present data suggesting that increased levels of ATP relative to GTP at the end of sporulation was the evolutionary pressure that drove the change in nucleotide preference in SpoIVA.
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by LC-MS data of nucleotide levels during sporulation shown in Figure 6.

claim: The free energy of the hydrolysis reaction involving the bond between the β- and the γ-phosphates is approximately 30 kJ/mol.
source: The free energy of the hydrolysis reaction involving the bond between the β- and the γ-phosphates is approximately 30 kJ/mol (Berg et al., 2007) and is used to drive a variety of energy-consuming biochemical reactions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to Berg et al., 2007.

claim: The relative intracellular abundance of ATP in a cell drove the evolution of motors to use it as an energy source.
source: One explanation for this dichotomy is that the relative intracellular abundance of ATP in a cell drove the evolution of motors to use it as an energy source (Bennett et al., 2009; Rudoni et al., 2001; Traut, 1994).
evidence: This is stated as an explanation from the literature with citations.

claim: The eukaryotic ATPase motor proteins myosin and kinesin are evolutionarily members of the TRAFAC class of GTPases, having emerged from an ancestral GTPase.
source: Consistent with that notion, the eukaryotic ATPase motor proteins myosin and kinesin are evolutionarily members of the TRAFAC class of GTPases, having emerged from an ancestral GTPase, but have switched their nucleotide specificity to utilizing the more abundant nucleotide ATP to perform their energy-intensive functions (Leipe et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a citation to Leipe et al., 2002.

claim: SpoIVA is exclusively found in sporulating members of the Firmicutes phylum.
source: In this report, we examine an unusual bacterial ATPase named SpoIVA (Ramamurthi and Losick, 2008; Roels et al., 1992) that is also from the TRAFAC class of GTPases and is exclusively found in sporulating members of the Firmicutes phylum (Castaing et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Castaing et al., 2013.

claim: Within the TRAFAC group, SpoIVA is closest to the Era GTPases.
source: We had previously shown that within the TRAFAC group, SpoIVA is closest to the Era GTPases (Castaing et al., 2013) which are switches involved in the maturation of 16S rRNA and assembly of the 30S ribosomal subunit and universally conserved across bacteria (Ji, 2016).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work (Castaing et al., 2013; Ji, 2016).

claim: Era GTPases are switches involved in the maturation of 16S rRNA and assembly of the 30S ribosomal subunit and universally conserved across bacteria.
source: We had previously shown that within the TRAFAC group, SpoIVA is closest to the Era GTPases (Castaing et al., 2013) which are switches involved in the maturation of 16S rRNA and assembly of the 30S ribosomal subunit and universally conserved across bacteria (Ji, 2016).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ji, 2016.

claim: SpoIVA emerged via a duplication event followed by rapid divergence from Era.
source: Given the universal conservation of Era among bacteria and the narrow conservation of SpoIVA, we proposed a model in which SpoIVA emerged via a duplication event followed by rapid divergence from Era (Castaing et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a model proposed in previous work (Castaing et al., 2013).

claim: The divergence from Era included the addition of two C-terminal domains in SpoIVA that are not present in Era.
source: This divergence from Era included not only multiple residue substitutions, but also the addition of two C-terminal domains in SpoIVA that are not present in Era (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: SpoIVA ATPase has the Era GTPase itself as its ancestor.
source: Further, the most parsimonious explanation of the phyletic patterns of SpoIVA and Era is that they are not formally sister groups where both diverged from a common ancestor; rather, SpoIVA ATPase, which emerged specifically in sporulating Firmicutes, has the Era GTPase itself as its ancestor.
evidence: This is an inference based on phyletic patterns.

claim: SpoIVA is a cytoskeletal protein that assembles into a static polymer in an ATP hydrolysis-dependent manner.
source: Unlike myosin and kinesin, SpoIVA is not a motor protein. Instead SpoIVA is a cytoskeletal protein that assembles into a static polymer in an ATP hydrolysis-dependent manner (Ramamurthi and Losick, 2008).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Ramamurthi and Losick, 2008.

claim: SpoIVA is essential for bacterial endospore formation.
source: SpoIVA is essential for bacterial endospore formation (Galperin et al., 2012; Roels et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Galperin et al., 2012 and Roels et al., 1992.

claim: Spores are encased in a proteinaceous shell, termed the spore 'coat', a complex structure that is composed of ~80 proteins.
source: Spores are encased in a proteinaceous shell, termed the spore 'coat', a complex structure that is composed of ~80 proteins (Driks and Eichenberger, 2016; Henriques and Moran, 2007; McKenney and Eichenberger, 2012).
evidence: This is stated with citations to multiple sources.

claim: Assembly of the coat begins with the construction of a basement layer, of which the major structural protein is SpoIVA.
source: Assembly of the coat begins with the construction of a basement layer, of which the major structural protein is SpoIVA (McKenney et al., 2010; Peluso et al., 2019; Price and Losick, 1999; Ramamurthi et al., 2006; Ramamurthi and Losick, 2008; Roels et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated with citations to multiple sources.

claim: SpoIVA polymerization requires ATP hydrolysis to form a nucleotide-free static polymer.
source: Unlike dynamic cytoskeletal proteins like actin and tubulin, where nucleotide binding drives polymerization and nucleotide hydrolysis is linked to polymer disassembly (Pollard and Goldman, 2018), SpoIVA polymerization requires ATP hydrolysis to form a nucleotide-free static polymer (Castaing et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Castaing et al., 2013 and Wu et al., 2015.

claim: The amino terminal half of the SpoIVA ATPase is the nucleotide-binding domain, which belongs to the TRAFAC class of P-loop GTPases.
source: The amino terminal half of the SpoIVA ATPase is the nucleotide-binding domain, which belongs to the TRAFAC class of P-loop GTPases (Figure 1A–C; Castaing et al., 2014; Castaing et al., 2013; Leipe et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with citations and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The classic TRAFAC GTPases which hydrolyze GTP contain a fourth motif (the so-called G4 motif), typically consisting of Asn and Lys separated by one residue before an Asp (NKxD) that confers guanine-binding specificity.
source: The classic TRAFAC GTPases which hydrolyze GTP contain a fourth motif (the so-called G4 motif), typically consisting of Asn and Lys separated by one residue before an Asp (NKxD) that confers guanine-binding specificity (Leipe et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Leipe et al., 2002.

claim: Crystal structures revealed direct interactions between the side chain of the Asp and the base of a bound GTP through two H-bonds.
source: Crystal structures revealed direct interactions between the side chain of the Asp and the base of a bound GTP through two H-bonds, and a coordination of a water molecule to the α-phosphate group of the bound nucleotide by the Lys (Knihtila et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Knihtila et al., 2015.

claim: Substitution of the Asp in the NKxD motif with Asn abolished the guanine-binding specificity of Ras and switched its specificity to xanthine.
source: Substitution of the Asp in this motif with Asn abolished the guanine-binding specificity of Ras, also a GTPase of the TRAFAC clade, and switched its specificity to xanthine (Kang et al., 1994; Weijland et al., 1994; Zhong et al., 1995).
evidence: This is stated with citations to multiple sources.

claim: Partial restoration of the NKxD motif and alteration of the SxE sequence resulted in a SpoIVA variant that hydrolyzed GTP in vitro slightly preferentially over ATP with reduced overall catalytic efficiency.
source: We found that partial restoration of the NKxD motif and alteration of the SxE sequence resulted in a SpoIVA variant that hydrolyzed GTP in vitro slightly preferentially over ATP with reduced overall catalytic efficiency, similar to the in vitro activity of the Era GTPase from which SpoIVA was likely derived in the ancestral sporulating Firmicute (Castaing et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Disrupting the NKxD motif in Era and introducing the SxE sequence into the G5 motif to mimic SpoIVA resulted in an Era variant that preferentially hydrolyzed ATP in vitro.
source: In parallel, disrupting the NKxD motif in Era and introducing the SxE sequence into the G5 motif to mimic SpoIVA resulted in an Era variant that preferentially hydrolyzed ATP in vitro.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The altered SpoIVA was able to harness the energy released by GTP or ATP hydrolysis to drive a necessary conformational change in the protein.
source: The altered SpoIVA was able to harness the energy released by GTP or ATP hydrolysis to drive a necessary conformational change in the protein but failed to ultimately polymerize specifically in the presence of GTP.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: SpoIVA forms an ADP-dependent multimer which is a necessary intermediate en route to functional SpoIVA polymerization.
source: We show that this was due to the inability of SpoIVA to form the equivalent of an ADP-dependent multimer in the presence of GTP, which we show is a necessary intermediate en route to functional SpoIVA polymerization.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The extant SpoIVA polymerizes more efficiently than the altered variant in the presence of lower ATP concentration.
source: Additionally, we provide evidence that the extant SpoIVA polymerizes more efficiently than the altered variant in the presence of lower ATP concentration, similar to what is present during the end of sporulation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: A pronounced reduction in intracellular GTP concentration relative to ATP during the late stages of sporulation could have driven the evolution of SpoIVA to utilize ATP instead of GTP to drive polymerization.
source: We propose that a pronounced reduction in intracellular GTP concentration relative to ATP during the late stages of sporulation could have driven the evolution of SpoIVA to utilize ATP instead of GTP to drive polymerization, a critical step in the morphogenesis of the spore cell surface.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings, particularly the nucleotide measurements in Figure 6.

claim: The Lys in the NKxD motif is consistently substituted by an alcoholic (S/T) residue in the SpoIVA family.
source: The next position is a K in most families of bona fide GTPases (Figure 1A) and the extended sidechain of this lysine forms the 'lateral wall' of the base-binding pocket (Figure 1D). Strikingly, this K is consistently substituted by an alcoholic (S/T) residue in the SpoIVA family.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: In SpoIVA, the conserved Asp in the G4 motif is mostly substituted by either of several polar residues, such as K, H, N, or R.
source: The next conserved position in G4 is the D, which is the most important determinant of guanine specificity (Figure 1D). In SpoIVA it is again mostly substituted by either of several polar residues, such as K, H, N, or R.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: In SpoIVA, the position corresponding to the conserved S in the G5 motif is less constrained and is usually either N, D, or S.
source: In the case of SpoIVA the position corresponding to the conserved S in the G5 motif is less constrained and is usually either N, D, or S.
evidence: This is stated based on sequence analysis.

claim: In SpoIVA, two residues downstream of S in the G5 motif, there is a position that is either acidic (D/E) or Q/N in 41% of the orthologs.
source: Two residues downstream of S, there is a position that contributes to the wall of the base-binding pocket. This position is not particularly conserved in TRAFAC GTPases as a whole but in SpoIVA is either acidic (D/E) or Q/N in 41% of the orthologs.
evidence: This is stated based on sequence analysis.

claim: The changes in the G4 (NKxD) and G5 (SxE) regions relative to the bona fide GTPases may have contributed to the emergence of ATP-specificity in SpoIVA.
source: Together, these observations suggested that the changes in the G4 (NKxD) and G5 (SxE) regions relative to the bona fide GTPases may have contributed to the emergence of ATP-specificity in SpoIVA (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from sequence analysis shown in Figure 1.

claim: Wild-type SpoIVA displayed a catalytic efficiency of 4.2 ± 0.9 min−1 mM−1 for ATP, compared to just 1.3 ± 0.8 min−1 mM−1 for GTP.
source: Wild-type (WT) SpoIVA displayed a catalytic efficiency of 4.2 ± 0.9 min−1 mM−1 for ATP, compared to just 1.3 ± 0.8 min−1 mM−1 for GTP, indicating that the protein hydrolyzed ATP approximately threefold more efficiently than GTP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2.

claim: Era hydrolyzed GTP with a catalytic efficiency of 0.7 ± 0.2 min−1 mM−1 upon incubation with an RNA oligonucleotide corresponding to the 16S rRNA sequence.
source: By comparison, Era did not display appreciable basal ATPase or GTPase activity, but upon incubation with an RNA oligonucleotide corresponding to the 16S rRNA sequence to which Era binds and which reportedly stimulates the enzymatic activity of Era (Meier et al., 2000; Tu et al., 2011), Era hydrolyzed GTP with a catalytic efficiency of 0.7 ± 0.2 min−1 mM−1, similar to the reported activity of E. coli Era (Tu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with citations to previous work.

claim: Era did not specifically hydrolyze ATP, as evidenced by the failure of the reaction to reach saturation and display Michaelis–Menten kinetics.
source: However, Era did not specifically hydrolyze ATP, as evidenced by the failure of the reaction to reach saturation and display Michaelis–Menten kinetics (Figure 2—figure supplement 1J, Figure 2A, 'I.D.' for 'indeterminable').
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1J.

claim: Restoring the Asp in the degenerate NKxD motif of SpoIVA did not significantly change the catalytic efficiencies of ATP or GTP hydrolysis.
source: Restoring the Asp in the degenerate NKxD motif of SpoIVA did not significantly change the catalytic efficiencies of ATP or GTP hydrolysis but restoring either the Lys or full NKxD motif in SpoIVA resulted in a ~2.5-fold increase in the catalytic efficiency for ATP and ~3.5-fold of that for GTP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2.

claim: Restoring either the Lys or full NKxD motif in SpoIVA resulted in a ~2.5-fold increase in the catalytic efficiency for ATP and ~3.5-fold of that for GTP hydrolysis.
source: Restoring the Asp in the degenerate NKxD motif of SpoIVA did not significantly change the catalytic efficiencies of ATP or GTP hydrolysis but restoring either the Lys or full NKxD motif in SpoIVA resulted in a ~2.5-fold increase in the catalytic efficiency for ATP and ~3.5-fold of that for GTP hydrolysis.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2.

claim: Restoring either the single Lys or the full NKxD motif resulted in decreased preference for ATP.
source: Restoring either the single Lys or the full NKxD motif resulted in decreased preference for ATP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Variants with restored Lys or full NKxD motif displayed an unusually high turnover rate that was ~10-fold higher for both NTPs than that displayed by WT SpoIVA.
source: Curiously, these variants also displayed an unusually high turnover rate that was ~10-fold higher for both NTPs than that displayed by WT SpoIVA (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Substituting both the Ser and Glu with Ala in the SxE sequence in the context of the restored NKxD motif resulted in lowered catalytic efficiencies, similar to WT SpoIVA.
source: Substituting both the Ser and Glu with Ala (to disrupt both positions with an amino acid with a short sidechain that is unlikely to perturb overall SpoIVA structure) in the context of the restored NKxD motif resulted in lowered catalytic efficiencies, similar to WT SpoIVA (Figure 2A,C: 'NKxD AxA').
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2A,C.

claim: Changing the SxE sequence to AxA increased the catalytic efficiency of the enzyme for GTP, resulting in drastically reduced specificity for ATP relative to WT SpoIVA.
source: This change also increased the catalytic efficiency of the enzyme for GTP, resulting in drastically reduced specificity for ATP relative to WT SpoIVA (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Combining a restoration of just the Asp residue of the degenerate NKxD motif with disruption of just the Glu of the SxE sequence resulted in an enzyme that displayed a similar catalytic efficiency to that of Era.
source: Finally, combining a restoration of just the Asp residue of the degenerate NKxD motif with disruption of just the Glu of the SxE sequence, resulted in an enzyme that displayed a similar catalytic efficiency to that of Era (Figure 2A, 'NSxD SxA'; hereafter referred to as 'SpoIVAGTPase'; Figure 2C) with a slight preference for GTP over ATP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2.

claim: The evolved Era variant (EraATPase) hydrolyzed ATP with a catalytic efficiency of 0.2 ± 0.1 min−1 mM−1 upon stimulation with the 16S rRNA fragment.
source: Similar to WT Era, the evolved Era (EraATPase) did not exhibit a basal NTPase activity, but upon stimulation with the 16S rRNA fragment, EraATPase hydrolyzed ATP with a catalytic efficiency of 0.2 ± 0.1 min−1 mM−1 (Figure 2A), but more curiously failed to specifically hydrolyze GTP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1K.

claim: EraATPase failed to specifically hydrolyze GTP.
source: Similar to WT Era, the evolved Era (EraATPase) did not exhibit a basal NTPase activity, but upon stimulation with the 16S rRNA fragment, EraATPase hydrolyzed ATP with a catalytic efficiency of 0.2 ± 0.1 min−1 mM−1 (Figure 2A), but more curiously failed to specifically hydrolyze GTP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1K.

claim: The Asp of the NKxD motif contributes to nucleotide specificity.
source: The mutational analyses therefore indicate that the Asp of the NKxD motif contributes to nucleotide specificity and that the substitution of Asp to Arg seen in the extant B. subtilis SpoIVA contributes to altering the nucleotide-binding pocket to discriminate against GTP in favor of ATP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The substitution of Asp to Arg in the extant B. subtilis SpoIVA contributes to altering the nucleotide-binding pocket to discriminate against GTP in favor of ATP.
source: The mutational analyses therefore indicate that the Asp of the NKxD motif contributes to nucleotide specificity and that the substitution of Asp to Arg seen in the extant B. subtilis SpoIVA contributes to altering the nucleotide-binding pocket to discriminate against GTP in favor of ATP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The Glu in the SxE sequence contributes to ATP hydrolysis specificity.
source: The Glu in the SxE sequence further contributes to ATP hydrolysis specificity and likely stabilizes the binding of ATP over GTP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational analysis data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Deletion of spoIVA resulted in a >108-fold and a ~106-fold reduction in the production of heat resistant spores and lysozyme-resistant spores, respectively.
source: Deletion of spoIVA resulted in a >108-fold and a ~106-fold reduction in the production of heat resistant spores and lysozyme-resistant spores, respectively (Roels et al., 1992, Figures 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 2), which could be complemented in trans by the introduction of WT spoIVA at an ectopic chromosomal locus.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figures 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, with citation to Roels et al., 1992.

claim: Expression of the NSxD variant complemented the spoIVA deletion.
source: In contrast, while expression of the NSxD variant (which displayed similar enzymatic activity as WT SpoIVA in vitro; Figures 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 2) complemented the spoIVA deletion, complementation by the hyperactive NKxR or NKxD variants resulted in >108-fold and ~104-fold decreases in the production of heat-resistant spores, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3.

claim: Complementation by the hyperactive NKxR or NKxD variants resulted in >108-fold and ~104-fold decreases in the production of heat-resistant spores, respectively.
source: In contrast, while expression of the NSxD variant (which displayed similar enzymatic activity as WT SpoIVA in vitro; Figures 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, Supplementary file 2) complemented the spoIVA deletion, complementation by the hyperactive NKxR or NKxD variants resulted in >108-fold and ~104-fold decreases in the production of heat-resistant spores, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3.

claim: Mutants that harbored a spoIVA allele containing a full substitution of the SxE sequence (resulting in AxA) largely failed to sporulate when the G4 motif also harbored alterations.
source: Similarly, mutants that harbored a spoIVA allele containing a full substitution of the SxE sequence (resulting in AxA) also largely failed to sporulate when the G4 motif also harbored alterations (Figures 3A and, Supplementary file 2; NKxD AxA and NKxR AxA).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SpoIVA variants were produced at levels similar to WT SpoIVA.
source: Immunoblot analysis of extracts prepared from sporulating cells revealed that these SpoIVA variants were produced at levels similar to WT SpoIVA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: SpoIVAGTPase (NSxD SxA) supported sporulation at near WT levels.
source: Interestingly, SpoIVAGTPase (NSxD SxA), which showed reduced but similar hydrolysis of ATP and GTP (Figure 2), supported sporulation at near WT levels (Figures 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figures 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: WT GFP-SpoIVA localized to the surface of the forespore.
source: WT GFP-SpoIVA localized to the surface of the forespore (Figure 3B,B'), as did the NSxD variant which sporulated at near-WT levels (Figure 3C,C').
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3B,B'.

claim: Restoring only the Lys of the degenerate G4 motif or restoring the entire NKxD motif in an otherwise WT SpoIVA resulted in the mis-localization of the variant as a focus near the surface of the forespore.
source: However, restoring only the Lys of the degenerate G4 motif or restoring the entire NKxD motif in an otherwise WT SpoIVA resulted in the mis-localization of the variant as a focus near the surface of the forespore.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3D–F,D'–F'.

claim: Various disruptions to the SxE sequence alone did not abrogate localization of the variant.
source: In contrast, various disruptions to the SxE sequence alone did not abrogate localization of the variant (Figure 3G–I,G'–I').
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3G–I,G'–I'.

claim: SpoIVAGTPase localized similar to WT.
source: Finally, SpoIVAGTPase localized similar to WT (Figure 3J–J'), consistent with its ability to support sporulation at a near-WT level.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 3J–J'.

claim: Co-incubation of SpoIVA with either ATP or GTP resulted in a different banding pattern in limited trypsin proteolysis, with full-length protein considerably resistant to degradation even after 10 min.
source: In the absence of nucleotide, SpoIVA was rapidly degraded, resulting in a characteristic banding pattern (Figure 4A). In contrast, co-incubation with either ATP or GTP resulted in a different banding pattern: most noticeably, the full-length protein was considerably resistant to degradation even after 10 min, suggestive of a massive conformational change in the protein upon hydrolysis of either nucleotide.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A conformational change in WT SpoIVA could be achieved at an approximately similar rate by hydrolysis of either ATP or GTP.
source: The disappearance of full-length SpoIVA was quantified to produce a decay rate which indicated that a conformational change in WT SpoIVA could be achieved at an approximately similar rate by hydrolysis of either by ATP or GTP (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Restoring the Lys alone, the entire NKxD motif alone, or in combination with the entirely disrupted SxE sequence (to AxA) resulted in a rapid decay rate in the presence of either ATP or GTP, indicating that these variants were unable to achieve the characteristic nucleotide-dependent conformational change.
source: In contrast, restoring the Lys alone, the entire NKxD motif alone, or in combination with the entirely disrupted SxE sequence (to AxA) resulted in a rapid decay rate in the presence of either ATP or GTP, indicating that these variants were unable to achieve the characteristic nucleotide-dependent conformational change, consistent with the observed in vivo defects of these variants (Figure 3, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4 and consistent with Figure 3.

claim: Variants harboring substitution of either the Ser or Glu singly or together in the SxE sequence with Ala or SpoIVAGTPase displayed a decay rate in the presence of either nucleotide that was more similar to WT SpoIVA.
source: However, variants harboring substitution of either the Ser or Glu singly or together in the SxE sequence with Ala or SpoIVAGTPase displayed a decay rate in the presence of either nucleotide that was more similar to WT SpoIVA, suggesting that that these variants were able to utilize the energy released from hydrolysis of either ATP or GTP to drive the conformational change in the protein that is a prerequisite for polymerization (Castaing et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4, with citation to Castaing et al., 2013.

claim: WT SpoIVA displayed an intermediate conformational change in the presence of ATP-γ-S or GTP-γ-S, suggesting that the protein bound, but did not hydrolyze, the nucleotide.
source: In the presence of ATP-γ-S or GTP-γ-S, WT SpoIVA displayed an intermediate conformational change suggesting that the protein bound, but did not hydrolyze, the nucleotide (Figure 2—figure supplement 1L, M), whereas SpoIVA harboring a Walker A disruption (SpoIVAA*, which prevents ATP binding [Ramamurthi and Losick, 2008]) did not undergo a similar conformational change (Figures 4C,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1L, M and Figures 4C,D.

claim: SpoIVA variant harboring a Sensor T disruption (SpoIVAT*) displayed a similar conformational change as WT SpoIVA in the presence of ATP-γ-S and GTP-γ-S.
source: Consistent with this result, the SpoIVA variant harboring a Sensor T disruption (SpoIVAT*, which binds, but does not hydrolyze ATP [Castaing et al., 2013]) displayed a similar conformational change as WT SpoIVA in the presence of ATP-γ-S and GTP-γ-S (Figures 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), and SpoIVAT* binding to ATP.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figures 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C, with citation to Castaing et al., 2013.

claim: The intermediate conformational change is likely due to nucleotide binding and not due to slow hydrolysis of the bound nucleotide.
source: Together, this suggested that this intermediate conformational change is likely due to nucleotide binding and not due to slow hydrolysis of the bound nucleotide.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings shown in Figure 4.

claim: The NKxD variant of SpoIVA displayed a conformational change in the presence of ATP-γ-S and GTP-γ-S similar to SpoIVAA*, suggesting that it did not stably undergo the initial conformational change that occurs upon binding the nucleotide.
source: Interestingly, the NKxD variant of SpoIVA, which exhibited elevated ATP and GTP hydrolysis levels (Figure 2A), displayed a conformational change in the presence of ATP-γ-S and GTP-γ-S similar to SpoIVAA* (Figures 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that it did not stably undergo the initial conformational change that occurs upon binding the nucleotide.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figures 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: WT SpoIVA and SpoIVAT* exhibited a similar intermediate conformational change when incubated with ADP or GDP, but not the full conformational change that occurred upon nucleotide hydrolysis.
source: WT SpoIVA and SpoIVAT* exhibited a similar intermediate conformational change when incubated with ADP or GDP, but not the full conformational change that occurred upon nucleotide hydrolysis (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Incubation of WT SpoIVA with either ADP-AlFx or GDP-AlFx produced a conformational change that was similar to that produced upon full hydrolysis of the nucleotide.
source: Curiously, incubation of WT SpoIVA with either ADP-AlFx or GDP-AlFx (Figure 4F) produced a conformational change that was similar to that produced upon full hydrolysis of the nucleotide (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The transition state mimics the activated state facilitated by ATP hydrolysis that is responsible for the conformational change.
